David thanked Anna for the honest advice. David bought a sweater online because it was much cheaper. On Sunday evenings, David reviews the notes from class. For example, the old Viking ship is in the museum.
The experience taught David more than any book could. There are always more possibilities than we expect. Little by little, things began to change. The gearbox needs an oil change.

David is saving money to buy a ticket to Rome. People around David often share different ideas about the city square. Anna always says that small steps matter more than big plans. In fact, the market is lively in the morning.

The pedestrian street has become an important part of daily life. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. David ordered dumplings and water at the pedestrian street last night. In fact, the card reader timed out twice.
David wrote down every idea in a small notebook. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. David believes that trying new things keeps life fresh.
